content.value_statement: Choosing the wrong input control can make Apple app workflows confusing and harder to access. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused HIG guidance for selection, text input, keyboards, and stateful controls.
actual_capabilities: Recommends controls for Boolean values, fixed choices, numeric ranges, and free-form text.
Compares toggles, segmented controls, sliders, steppers, pickers, combo boxes, and token fields.
Explains when changes should apply immediately or wait for form confirmation.
Highlights platform differences for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS.
Adds accessibility guidance for labels, VoiceOver context, state visibility, and validation messages.
References virtual keyboard options for email, URL, number, search, phone, and custom entry.
limitations: It provides design guidance, not production-ready UI code.
It does not replace testing with platform accessibility tools and real users.
It depends on the included HIG reference excerpts and may not cover newer Apple updates.
It cannot validate visual implementations without screenshots, prototypes, or source code.

use_cases.title: Choose Form Controls
use_cases.description: Select the right control for settings, onboarding, checkout, or profile forms before building the interface.

use_cases.title: Review Apple Platform UI
use_cases.description: Check whether an existing control pattern matches HIG expectations for state, labels, and platform behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan Accessible Data Entry
use_cases.description: Define keyboard types, validation timing, labels, and VoiceOver support for text-heavy workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Control
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to recommend the best Apple HIG control for a Boolean setting, five options, or a numeric range. Explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Alternatives
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare a segmented control, picker, and pop-up button for this option list: [describe options]. Include state and accessibility notes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review this Apple app form: [paste fields and platforms]. Flag mismatched controls, weak labels, validation issues, and keyboard choices.

prompt_templates.title: Create Control Guidelines
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create reusable control guidance for our Apple design system. Cover selection patterns, text entry, validation, accessibility, and platform differences.

output_examples.input: A settings row enables or disables iCloud sync.
output_examples.output: Use a switch in the list row. The row label provides context, and the change should apply immediately.

output_examples.input: A macOS preferences pane lets people choose one of four export formats.
output_examples.output: Use radio buttons or a segmented control. Prefer radio buttons when labels need more space or explanation.

output_examples.input: A signup form asks for email, phone, and a one-time code.
output_examples.output: Use email, phone, and number keyboard types. Show validation after editing, and keep labels clear for VoiceOver.

best_practices: Start by identifying the data type, option count, platform, and commit behavior.
Prefer standard system controls unless a custom control solves a clear task-specific problem.
Always describe visible state, validation timing, labels, and accessibility traits.
anti_patterns: Using switches for every Boolean choice, even when a checkbox or button toggle fits better.
Forcing long option lists into segmented controls with crowded labels.
Choosing custom keyboards or controls without a clear user benefit.

faq.question: Does this skill generate code?
faq.answer: No. It gives design recommendations and implementation considerations, but it does not produce complete UI code by itself.

faq.question: Which platforms does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS guidance found in the included HIG references.

faq.question: Can it help with accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It prompts for labels, state clarity, VoiceOver context, validation messages, and standard control behavior.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses local reference files. External links are citations and attribution in Markdown.

faq.question: How should I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Ask Claude Code or Codex to apply the skill while reviewing a form, settings screen, or input workflow.

faq.question: Can it replace Apple's official docs?
faq.answer: No. Use it as a focused assistant, then verify final decisions against current Apple documentation and platform testing.
